chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me regarding the shroud of Abu Ubayda al-Hazza': 'Indeed, the embalming material is camphor, but go and do as the people do.'

key_terms.النَّاسُ: The people, referring to the general custom or practice of the community
key_terms.الْحَذَّاءِ: The cobbler, a kunya (nickname) for Abu Ubayda
key_terms.الْحَنُوطُ: Embalming material or substance used for preserving the body
key_terms.الْكَافُورُ: Camphor, a specific aromatic substance used in burial

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using camphor for embalming the deceased in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the specific religious recommendation of using camphor for embalming and the flexibility to adopt local customs for the general shrouding process, reflecting the Shia principle of balancing ritual precision with cultural adaptability. This hadith highlights the juristic concept of 'urf' (custom) in funeral rites, allowing for communal harmony while maintaining core spiritual obligations. It underscores the practical wisdom of the Imams in guiding the community without imposing rigid uniformity where flexibility is permissible.
